_comment: Failure-criteria thresholds for the uSTOL CRUISE ROLL/YAW DOUBLET stability campaign (aws_monte_carlo_9_nodt / mission_ustol_10_cruise_nodt). This is a DELIBERATE-MANEUVER test flown at cruise (~100 m), NOT the takeoff->cruise->land mission, so the landing-mission criteria in failure_criteria_config.json are wrong here (they flag the intended doublet excursions as failures). build_dashboard_data.py auto-selects THIS file when the campaign carries the doublet outcome fields (stab_* / roll_worst_* / yaw_*). Tune the thresholds to your real limits.
_instructions: Same engine/kinds as failure_criteria_config.json: scalar | timeseries | oscillation | envelope.

Doublet outcome scalars (stab_*, roll_worst_*, yaw_*) come straight from result.json. Booleans flow through as 1.0/0.0, so 'fail if departed' is {metric:stab_departed, max:0.5} and 'fail if NOT settled' is {metric:stab_settled, min:0.5}.

ALTITUDE-LOSS GUARD (test_alt_floor): the runner's settle/departure logic checks ONLY roll angle + yaw rate, never altitude, so an aircraft upset into a wings-level DESCENT sinks to the ground yet is still reported land_result='settled', stab_departed=false. test_alt_floor catches those: it FAILS any case whose minimum test-window altitude fell below the floor. Keep this until the runner itself gains an altitude check.

recover-time caveat: roll_worst_recover_s / yaw_worst_recover_s are -1.0 when no doublet recovered (e.g. the case departed before completing the sequence). A bare 'max' bound would read -1 as good; that edge is covered because such cases already FAIL on stab_departed. Among completed cases the value is a real positive recovery time.

DROPPED vs the landing config and WHY: all takeoff/touchdown/approach/flare criteria (wrong mission); descent_rate + flight_path_gamma whole-flight (the doublets intentionally pitch/sink/swing gamma); all (V,gamma) safe_envelope_* criteria (the only exported band is cfg32=flap20 STOL, but cruise flies clean flap0 -> 99.8% false-fail; export safe_envelope_cfg18.csv from flight_envelopes.m and re-add scoped to CLIMB/CRUISE to restore them).
load_factor / AoA limits are RAISED vs the landing config because banking to +/-20 deg legitimately pulls g and raises AoA; they now flag only genuine over-stress / stall, not the maneuver itself.

criteria._doublet_outcome_comment: Primary verdict drivers — the actual point of the campaign. A departure, an abort, or a loss of test altitude is a hard FAIL; sluggish tracking/recovery is degraded.
criteria._structural_comment: Load factor scored on PERCENTILE-FILTERED metrics (load_factor_total_p95 / load_factor_nz_p05, built from the flight-log RAW_IMU load factor). The runner's raw peak (max_load_factor_total / min_load_factor_nz) is a single-sample specific-force reading that carries SITL IMU vibration spikes to 5-6 g the airframe cannot aerodynamically reach, so it tripped every case; the 95th/5th percentile isolates genuinely-sustained load. For a stricter check switch the metric to _p99 / _p01. +/-20 deg bank needs ~1.06 g steady; transients higher.
criteria._climb_comment: The open-loop climb to cruise still happens and is worth grading. Gated to the established climb (alt_agl in [5,90] m) so the rotation transient and the level-off to 100 m don't false-flag.
criteria._cruise_comment: Scoped to the CRUISE label = the clean settle BEFORE the doublets begin, so it grades the trimmed starting condition (not the maneuvers, which are labelled ROLL/YAW).
criteria._rate_comment: Body-rate ceilings, generous for a maneuver test (roll doublets legitimately spin up p). Catch only runaway rates.
criteria._aoa_comment: Stall guard, widened to +/-12 deg and demoted to degraded for the maneuver test; gated on TAS>=6 so ground/near-zero-airspeed samples (AoA undefined) are excluded.
criteria._oscillation_comment: Control-oscillation health, per axis, verdict driven by the COMMAND channel with the actual surface + body rate as diagnostics. Spectrum 'phases' include the doublet phases (ROLL/YAW) and the settles (CRUISE/RETURN) so a limit-cycle during or after the maneuvers is caught. Only <~5 Hz is visible at 10 Hz logging.
